recipes.name: Carolyn's Oh-So-Easy Cherry Cobbler
ingredients_raw: 1 (15 ounce) can pitted tart red cherries, drained with liquid reserved

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Prepare a 9x9-inch baking dish with cooking spray.
Stir the liquid from the cherries and 1/2 cup sugar together in a small glass bowl; heat in the microwave until the sugar is dissolved, 1 to 2 minutes. Set aside.

Stir the baking mix, 1/2 cup sugar, and milk together in a separate small bowl; mix until you get a moist batter. Spread the mixture in an even layer in the bottom of the prepared baking dish. Spread the cherries evenly over the batter. Slowly pour the cherry juice over the cherries.
Bake in the preheated oven until lightly browned, 25 to 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Carolyn's Oh-So-Easy Cherry Cobbler
raw_recipe.description: Canned tart cherries, buttermilk, cherries, and buttermilk baking mix are all you need to make this quick and easy dessert.

review.reviewBody: Very yummy and satisfying to a sweet lover. However, I made these changes to the recipe, only because I had this on hand: I used a 1/2 of 16 oz bag of frozen, mixed berries (raspberries; blueberries; blackberries; strawberries,cut up)and sprinkled 1/4 cup sugar on the fruit before thawing in the microwave. This produced a syrup with the fruit. I combined a 1/4 cup of sugar with 1/2 cup water to pour over the fruit. When I added the fruit to the batter, I poured the juice it made with it, also. Next time, I'm going to double the fruit and use Splenda and light Bisquick mix for the batter.

This is wonderful. I doubled the recipe batter mixture, which is actually between a batter and a dough following the recipe. I used the larger Pyrex size pan to pour the dough into, and just opened a can of Comstock Cherry Pie Filling and poured it on top. I used 1/2 cup Keebler Graham Cracker Crumbs and added 1 T sugar to them. Poured this over the top of Cherry Pie Filling. Cooked for 20 minutes and then ran a knife through the mix to stir it up a bit. Baked total of about an hour. It came up some crispy, some gooey, and some chewy. Very Nice with just a cup of milk to drink with it. Thank you for sharing this simple work of art that so easily adapts to whatever we have on hand. LOVE IT!

This recipe was great in a pinch. I used 2 cans of tart pie cherries, halved both the sugar quantities and used 2 cups bisquick, and 1 cup milk. I spilled about 1/4 cup of the cherry juice on the floor and the cobbler still turned out fine, in fact it was a little runny on the bottom. Next time I may try a tablespoon of flour or cornstarch. I baked it in a 9x13" at 350 for 25 min and then broiled it at 550 for 5 min and the top is nice and golden. It was superb, will definitely make again. Guests raved about it. Thank you!

I made this but made it easier! I poured 2 cans of cherry pie filling in a 9" x13" pan. I then sprinkled a box of WHITE cake mix on top, as evenly distributed as possible. Then, I cut up in small slices 1 & 1/2 sticks of real unsalted butter & arranged them all over the top of the cake mix. I put the pan in a pre-heated 350• oven & baked it for 1 hr & 5 min. (Depends on how accurate ur oven temp is!)! The white vs yellow cake makes ALL the difference! Makes for a crunchier more cobbler-like appearance & it just tastes GREAT!!

I absolutely loved it. I used frozen cherries a large bag. Defrosted in microwave with 1/2 cup sugar which created the juice I needed. Then strained and cooked juice as directed. I put cherries in a strainer and they drained some more. I doubled the recipe for the bisquick mix. I used regular not buttermilk. I added only 1/2 cup of sugar. Mixed as directed with a cup of 1% milk. Spread batter in bottom of pan and arranged cherries over the top. To the juice that drained from the cherries I added a tablespoon of cornstarch and mixed in with the microwaved juice and sugar. Poured over the top of batter and cherries. Baked for 35 minutes . It turned out perfect. I was so surprised. I thought it would be soupy because of all the juice. But the cornstarch helped I figured. Best cherry cobbler I ever made.

The cherries on our trees were ripe! I pitted them and they seemed wet so I tossed them with 1 tbsp. of cornstarch like my Mom used to do. I was out of milk but had coconut milk on hand. Turned out great.

As advertised, very easy recipe. Saw comment about it being too soft, so added a bit of melted butter to generously sprayed pan before adding batter. Cooked an extra 10 min. Came out perfect with crisp edges. Used 16oz bag of frozen cherries, heated in the microwave with the sugar, and it made lots of liquid. Didn't think it would gel without cornstarch, but it did. Could easily double the fruit next time. Could do the same with any fruit. Must have vanilla ice cream with it. Great with a splash of rum or red wine over the top.

OK...so I made a couple of changes: increased pancake mix to 3/4 cups, increased milk to 1 cup, added 1 teaspoon almond extract tossed with the cherries, melted 1/4 cup of butter in 9 x13 " baking dish in the oven before pouring batter over. Then proceeded with the recipe as written. Served warm with whipped cream....heavenly.

I doubled this to use in a 9x13. I had frozen cherries so I just sprinkled them with the sugar and defrosted them in the microwave. That made the syrup when they were finished thawing. The only other difference I made was to add a bit more sugar to the batter and to melt a stick of butter in the pan and then pour the batter on that followed by the fruit and syrup. My family loved this but my 7 year old son ADORED it, I ended up getting only 1 piece. Thanks for the recipe!

Really great! I needed to make a quick dessert for a get-together and didn't have enough flour for a cherry pie. So I came across this, had the Bisquick, and threw it together! SO easy! I actually doubled the recipe, baked it for about 15 minutes longer in a 9x13. I also added some almond extract to the syrup mixture before pouring it on top of the batter and cherries. Will definitely be making this again sometime!

I agree with Tom, this was an uneditable mess! I threw it away. I started over and somewhat changed the recipe. I used Pearl milling pancake mix and Cherry pie filling. One cup pancake mix, half cup sugar, and half cup+ milk. I put the cherry pie filling in one tablespoon at a time in different spots. 350° - 25min. This was fantastic recipe.

Sometimes my brain goes on vacation when I (attempt to) cook. Haha. Too late, I realized the cherry pie filling didn't need the extra sugar called for. Canned cherry pie filling is easier to find than canned cherries where I live. Anyway, I went ahead and added some lemon juice to the liquid and then less sugar to the pancake batter. This is a sensational recipe if you pay attention to what you're doing or even partially as I do. It still works. Can't wait to make it correctly next time!! Also, pouring the cream of your choice over the cobbler instead of ice cream can help cut the sweetness. Huzzah!!

(7.29.23) Not sure what happened here, but I got no rise on the batter, and it was extremely “wet” with cherry juice (but that juice did taste good). I made one substitution with buttermilk because I was out of milk, but I certainly wouldn’t think that would create any issues. The batter was very thick and difficult to spread out in the pan, like there wasn’t enough, and I also think an 8” dish would work better than a 9”. It tasted OK, but certainly not what I’d expect in a cobbler.

I don't understand the raves. The recipe clearly says put the batter on the bottom. If you do, it does not make anything close to what is shown in the pictures. It's barely edible, but mostly a gummy mess.

Super easy and super tasty!
I used pie filling and it was great.
Too Easy
Added 1/2 t almond extract and used buttermilk instead of milk. Great and easy. I will make again.
Easy and delicious. I used a jar of cherries from Aldi and also added some frozen strawberries. Don't be scared of all the liquid on top, it works great.

I have made this numerous late nights, and I'm here to tell you it will make your tongue smack your brains out! Top it warm with vanilla ice cream to really indulge yourself. I've also made it with canned apples (NOT PIE FILLING) for my husband, and he loved it. I think canned peaches would work well too.

Have made this twice this week! The second time, I brought the cherry juice and sugar to a low boil on the stove, for about 5 minutes then let cool for a few minutes. Worked out better, I think; kinda like a thin cherry jam. I also doubled the recipe and made in a 9"x11" pan the second time. Rave reviews!! I think it turned out better doubling and using a slightly bigger pan; more loft.

I double this recipe and baked in a 9x13 pan. Bake time was a little longer to achieve the desired browning of the crust. This was very sweet and if I were to make it again I would reduce the amount of sugar substantially and probably add a litte salt to the crust mixture. Thanks for sharing your recipe!
